what: Bond cash flows and the value equation
title: Bonds, Duration, Convexity, and Immunization
text: Consider conventional bond face value F, coupon rate r per coupon period, redemption value C, effective yield per coupon period, n remaining coupon periods. periodic coupon Fr. Taking valuation date time 0, future cash flows Fr,\; Fr,\; \ldots,\; Fr+C. Therefore, P = Fr(v+v^2+\cdots+v^n)+Cv^n, v=(1+)^{-1}. Since coupon payments form annuity-immediate, P = Fr\,a_{\overline{n}|} + Cv^n. Equivalently, P = Fr\frac{1-(1+)^{-n}}{} + C(1+)^{-n}. ordinary equation value applied level stream coupons plus single redemption payment. coupon rate, yield, number periods must refer time unit.

title: Bonds, Duration, Convexity, and Immunization

Hence, P = 45{,}000a_{\overline{12}|0.05} + 1{,}000{,}000(1.05)^{-12} = 955{,}683.74. constructing equation value move computational representation. bond_cash_flows() represents contractual payments. determine bond price. valuation basis introduced separately. package result reproduces analytical value. comparison verifies computational implementation follows actuarial equation established independently.

what: Duration and convexity of a cash-flow stream
title: Bonds, Duration, Convexity, and Immunization
text: payments C_j times t_j, P() = \sum_j C_j(1+)^{-t_j}. Define present-value weights w_j() = \frac{C_j(1+)^{-t_j}}{P()}. positive cash flows, Macaulay duration D_{\text{Mac}}() = \sum_j t_jw_j(), modified duration D_{\text{mod}}() = -\frac{1}{P()}\frac{dP()}{di} = \frac{D_{\text{Mac}}()}{1+}. Thus, \frac{\Delta P}{P} \approx -D_{\text{mod}}\Delta . Relative convexity C() = \frac{1}{P()}\frac{d^2P()}{di^2}, second-order approximation \frac{\Delta P}{P} \approx -D_{\text{mod}}\Delta + \frac12 C(\Delta )^2. Duration gives first-order approximation; convexity adds effect curvature.

title: Level annuity factor a-angle-n — a_angle
text: Supported timing conventions: "immediate": annuity-immediate discrete payments. "due": annuity-due discrete payments. "continuous": continuous annuity. discrete annuities, k number payments per year, payments made every \(1/k\) year. function returns annuity factor, assuming unit payment payment time. Deferment supported h. discrete annuities, deferment must align payment grid, , \(hk\) must integer. perpetuity = TRUE, infinite-term annuity factor returned. function follows compact actuarial notation used throughout tidyactuarial: n: annuity term; k: payment frequency; : interest rate; i_type: interest-rate type; m: conversion frequency nominal rates; h: deferment period. function first converts supplied rate equivalent annual effective interest rate using standardize_interest. finite discrete annuities: $$a_{\overline{n|}} = \frac{1 - v^n}{}$$ due annuities: $$\ddot{}_{\overline{n|}} = (1+)a_{\overline{n|}}$$ continuous annuities: $$\bar{}_{\overline{n|}} = \frac{1 - e^{-\delta n}}{\delta}$$ generally, let \(N=nk\), let \(b=0\) immediate payments \(b=1\) due payments. deferred discrete factor $$\sum_{j=1}^{N} \exp\{-\delta[h+(j-b)/k]\}.$$ discrete payment one unit, whereas continuous annuity pays one unit per year. continuous deferred factor \(\int_h^{h+n} e^{-\delta t}\,dt\). original log accumulation rate retained even annual effective equivalent rounds -1 overflows. Geometric sums continuous integrals use stable logarithmic formulas exact zero-rate limits, rather replacing small nonzero rate zero. Perpetuities require strictly positive rate, without numerical lower cutoff. Let \(j\) effective yield per coupon period, \(k\) number coupon payments per year, let cash flows \(C_r\) occur coupon periods \(r = 1, \dots, N\). \(v = 1/(1+j)\) \(P = \sum_r C_r v^r\), discrete convexity coupon periods $$C_p = \frac{1}{P} \frac{\sum_{r=1}^{N} C_r r(r+1) v^r}{(1+j)^2}.$$ Discrete convexity years \(C_p / k^2\). sensitivity nominal annual yield \(z=kj\); generally relative second derivative respect annual effective yield \(=(1+j)^k-1\). passing convexity immunize_duration_convexity(), apply chain rule described compute convexity_cash_flow() annual cash-flow times. second-order sensitivity bond price changes yield per period. title: Bootstrap a spot yield curve from instrument prices — bootstrap_spot_curve
text: instrument \(j\), maturity \(t_j\), dirty price \(P_j\), cash flows \(CF_{j,k}\), price identity $$P_j = \sum_{k < j} CF_{j,k} v(t_k) + CF_{j,j} v(t_j).$$ Hence new discount factor recovered exactly $$v(t_j) = \frac{P_j - \sum_{k < j} CF_{j,k} v(t_k)}{CF_{j,j}}.$$ annual effective spot rate $$i_{t_j} = v(t_j)^{-1/t_j} - 1.$$ input row represents one instrument; t cf list-columns. Repeated payment times within instrument combined, allowing coupon redemption flows produced bond_cash_flows(). Instruments processed increasing final positive-payment time, input row order. Zero cash flows ignored. Duplicate final maturities, missing earlier discount-factor nodes, zero negative residual prices, nonpositive terminal cash flows rejected. exact triangular bootstrapping: interpolate, extrapolate, fit curve, estimate least-squares solution. annual effective spot rate can negative; discount factor must positive. Input prices cash flows must use monetary units. positive finite discount factor annual effective rate -1 must representable. Rounded input prices can make small terminal residual ill-conditioned; tolerance silently replaces nonpositive residual. repricing_error reports recomputed floating-point discrepancy, independent accuracy guarantee convergence test.

title: Bootstrap a spot yield curve from instrument prices — bootstrap_spot_curve
code: # Recover a known 1-, 2-, and 3-year annual effective spot curve. t <- 1:3 i <- c(0.04, 0.045, 0.05) v <- (1 + i)^(-t) instruments <- tibble::tibble(   instrument = c("Zero 1Y", "Coupon 2Y", "Coupon 3Y"),   price = c(100 * v[1],             5 * v[1] + 105 * v[2],             6 * v[1] + 6 * v[2] + 106 * v[3]),   t = list(1, c(1, 2), c(1, 2, 3)),   cf = list(100, c(5, 105), c(6, 6, 106)) ) curve <- instruments |> bootstrap_spot_curve() curve #> # A tibble: 3 × 9 #>   instrument     t price known_pv terminal_cf     v      i repriced_price #>   <chr>      <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>          <dbl> #> 1 Zero 1Y        1  96.2     0            100 0.962 0.0400           96.2 #> 2 Coupon 2Y      2 101.      4.81         105 0.916 0.045           101.  #> 3 Coupon 3Y      3 103.     11.3          106 0.864 0.050           103.  #> # ℹ 1 more variable: repricing_error <dbl> yield_curve(t = curve$t, i = curve$i) #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>   t         i         v         i_effective #>   <list>    <list>    <list>    <list>      #> 1 <dbl [3]> <dbl [3]> <dbl [3]> <dbl [3]>

title: Expected future lifetime from an annual life table — e_x
text: Curtate life expectancy (Finan, Section 23.7): $$e_x = \sum_{k=1}^{\omega - x} {}_k p_x = \frac{1}{\ell_x}   \sum_{k=1}^{\omega - x} \ell_{x+k}.$$ \(t\)-year temporary curtate expectancy (Finan, Sec. 23.7): $$e_{x:\overline{t}|} = \sum_{k=1}^{t} {}_k p_x.$$ Complete life expectancy (Finan, Section 23.3): $$\breve{e}_x = \int_0^{\omega - x} {}_t p_x \, dt =   \frac{T_x}{\ell_x}.$$ integral decomposed year--year. Within year, within-year survival integral \(\int_0^s {}_u p_y \, du\) evaluated closed form selected fractional-age assumption (Finan, Section 24): UDD (Sec. 24.1): \(\int_0^s {}_u p_y \, du = s - \frac{1}{2} s^2 q_y\) CF (Sec. 24.2): \(\int_0^s {}_u p_y \, du = (1 - p_y^s) / (-\ln p_y)\) Balducci (Sec. 24.3): \(\int_0^s {}_u p_y \, du = \frac{p_y}{q_y} \ln \left( \frac{p_y + q_y s}{p_y} \right)\) Integrals use stable exponential/logarithmic increments small durations. Extinct cohorts contribute zero later intervals, even conditional probabilities undefined. CF/Balducci zero-survival interval integral zero; UDD retains linear decline. Unknown survivor counts propagate missing expectations. annual probabilities must derived survivor counts, survival uses direct count ratio rather \(1-q_y\). logarithm retains CF integral even annual ratio floating-point range. UDD, complete expectancy satisfies well-known approximation (Finan, Example 20.24): $$\breve{e}_x \approx e_x + \frac{1}{2}.$$

title: Kaplan–Meier survival curve and a lifetable-style life table — km_lifetable
text: resulting life table intended *experience-based* (empirical) life tables actuarial/demographic contexts (e.g., cohort studies, population indicators). replacement graduated/regulatory tables smoothing, extrapolation, product-specific selection effects required. **Kaplan–Meier estimator.** observed event time \(t_j\): $$\hat S(t) = \prod_{t_j \le t} \left(1 - \frac{d_j}{n_j}\right)$$ \(n_j\) risk set size \(d_j\) number events. Greenwood's variance: $$\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat S(t)) = \hat S(t)^2 \sum_{t_j \le t} \frac{d_j}{n_j(n_j - d_j)}.$$ Pointwise confidence intervals use log(-log) transformation. **Life table mapping.** interval \([x, x + \Delta)\): $$\ell_x = \text{radix} \cdot \hat S(x), \quad d_x = \ell_x -   \ell_{x+\Delta}, \quad q_x = d_x / \ell_x.$$ Exposure \(L_x = \int_x^{x+\Delta} \ell(t)\,dt\) computed using selected fractional-age assumption (Finan, Section 24): UDD (Finan, Sec. 24.1):     \(L_x \approx \tfrac{\ell_x + \ell_{x+\Delta}}{2} \Delta\) CF (constant force, Finan, Sec. 24.2):     \(L_x = \Delta \cdot (\ell_x - \ell_{x+\Delta}) /     \ln(\ell_x / \ell_{x+\Delta})\) Balducci (Finan, Sec. 24.3):     \(L_x = \Delta \cdot \ell_x \ell_{x+\Delta} /     (\ell_x - \ell_{x+\Delta}) \cdot \ln(\ell_x / \ell_{x+\Delta})\) Additional columns follow Finan, Sections 23.3, 23.8–23.9: \(T_x = \sum_{k \ge x} L_k\): total expected years lived     age \(x\) (Finan, Sec. 23.3). \(\mathring{e}_x = T_x / \ell_x\): complete life expectancy     (Finan, Sec. 23.3). \(m_x = d_x / L_x\): central death rate (Finan, Sec. 23.9). \(a_x = (L_x - \ell_{x+\Delta}\Delta) / d_x\): mean time     lived within interval die, years (fraction     interval width differs one). Undefined deaths. Nonfinite time/entry rows omitted warning; remaining sample must nonempty. Breaks sorted deduplicated. Beyond last observation, KM step held constant (tail extrapolation fitted). CF/Balducci exposure interval ending zero survival uses zero limit; positive deaths zero exposure give infinite central mortality. Confidence intervals remain undefined survival zero one. Standard errors intervals use Greenwood sums directly, preserving small positive survival estimates without fixed survival floor. delayed entry risk set uses existing inclusive convention entry <= time; deliberate convention tied entries/events. lifetable component may arbitrary interval widths: annual consumers t_px require conversion annual grid needed endpoint survivors; class alone certify conversion.

title: Build an annual life table (tidy tibble) from lx, qx, px, or mx — lifetable
text: table can built one : lx (survivors), qx (one-year death probabilities), px (one-year survival probabilities), mx (central death rates), function compute remaining columns consistently: dx, qx, px, mx. multiple inputs provided, priority : lx > qx > px > mx. lx provided together qx, cross-consistency validated (must agree via \(q_x = (\ell_x - \ell_{x+1}) / \ell_x\)). default, table actuarially closed omega: $$\ell_{\omega+1} = 0 \Rightarrow d_{\omega} = \ell_{\omega}       \Rightarrow q_{\omega} = 1 \Rightarrow p_{\omega} = 0.$$ life table follows standard actuarial construction described Finan, Sections 22–24 (Exam MLC preparation). basic identities (Finan, Section 22): $$\ell_x = \ell_0 \cdot s(x), \quad d_x = \ell_x - \ell_{x+1},       \quad q_x = d_x / \ell_x, \quad p_x = \ell_{x+1} / \ell_x.$$ \(a_x\) mean fraction year lived die, exposure \(L_x = \ell_{x+1} + a_x d_x\) \(m_x = d_x / L_x\). Consequently, $$m_x = \frac{q_x}{1 - (1 - a_x) q_x}, \quad       q_x = \frac{m_x}{1 + (1 - a_x) m_x}$$ UDD (ax = 0.5) reduces classical formula \(m_x = q_x / (1 - 0.5 \, q_x)\) (Finan, Section 24.1). arises UDD, \(L_x = \ell_x - \tfrac{1}{2} d_x\), therefore \(m_x = d_x / L_x\). terminal age \(\omega\) close = TRUE, closure forces \(q_\omega = 1\), \(p_\omega = 0\), \(d_\omega = \ell_\omega\). positive terminal survivors, \(L_\omega = a_x \ell_\omega\) \(m_\omega = 1/a_x\), 2 UDD (ax = 0.5). ax = 0, zero-exposure limit \(m_\omega = \infty\); ax = 1, \(m_\omega = 1\). Infinite mx inputs remain unsupported; limit can obtained lx qx.

text: output follows tidyactuarial conventions includes columns x, qx, px, lx, dx, Lx, Tx, ex, mx. function follows compact actuarial notation used throughout tidyactuarial: x denotes age, l0 denotes starting radix, a_x denotes average fraction year lived dying age interval, qx denotes one-year death probability, px = 1 - qx. Ratios use actual denominators: mx = dx / Lx ex = Tx / lx. Positive deaths zero exposure give infinite mx; extinct cohorts zero numerators denominators give NaN undefined ratios. Heligman-Pollard follows eight-parameter odds specification Heligman Pollard (1980), section 2.1, equation (1), doi:10.1017/S0020268100040257 . title: Generate a tidy life table from a theoretical mortality law — mortality_law_table
text: Exponential: \(\mu_x = \lambda\). Gompertz: \(\mu_x = Bc^x\). Makeham: \(\mu_x = + Bc^x\). Weibull: \(\mu_x = (shape/scale)(x/scale)^{shape-1}\). Logistic: \(\mu_x = (+ Bc^x)/(1 + Cc^x)\). DeMoivre: finite lifetime law   \(q_x = 1/(\omega - x)\) \(x < \omega\). Beta: scaled lifetime model   \(X/\omega \sim Beta(\alpha,\beta)\). HeligmanPollard: eight-parameter odds model   \(q_x/p_x = ^{(x+B)^C} + D\exp(-E(\log x-\log F)^2) + GH^x\),   F_hp denoting \(F\).

title: Par coupon rate implied by a spot yield curve — par_rate
text: bond face value \(F > 0\), redemption \(R\), term \(n\), \(k\) coupon payments per year, price equation $$P = (F c/k) \sum_{j=1}^{nk} v(j/k) + R v(n).$$ Setting dirty price \(P = F\) solving nominal annual coupon rate gives $$c_{par} = k [F - R v(n)] / [F \sum_{j=1}^{nk} v(j/k)].$$ redemption equals face value, reduces $$c_{par} = k [1 - v(n)] / \sum_{j=1}^{nk} v(j/k).$$ Spot inputs use annual effective rates default, \(v(t) = (1 + i_t)^{-t}\). supported interest conventions converted using discount_factor_spot(). calculation uses observed nodes: every coupon date must match one curve maturity; interpolation extrapolation. Small floating-point discrepancies within tol accepted identical dates. Input can (1) numeric vectors t , (2) data frame numeric t columns, bootstrap_spot_curve() output, (3) tibble t list-columns, yield_curve() output. third form row describes one curve, input columns retained. n, face, k, R may scalars one value per curve. single curve, n = NULL uses largest observed maturity. coupon rate can negative implied financial terms require ; function impose contractual zero floor. model assumes regular coupons paid arrears, stub periods, accrued interest, deterministic redemption maturity. Calculation separates dimensionless rate monetary amounts uses original log spot growth maturity retain small coupon rates. text: prospective reserve $${}_tV = \operatorname{APV}_t(\text{future benefits}) - P^{(k)}\operatorname{APV}_t(\text{future premium annuity}).$$ [annuity_xy()] assigns amount `1 / k` payment, `P` annualized actual installment `P / k`. Future installments use selected annuity method; current installment exact `P / k`. Last-survivor recursion tracks -alive single-survivor state separately. recursive statuses use backward conditional transition identities, direct annual `lx` decrements original log interest basis. avoids forward cancellation loss effective-rate conversion. Unreachable transitions contribute exactly zero. recursion's existing timing deferment restrictions retained. Conditional states whose reserves overflow double precision generally recoverable.

title: Specify an individual claim severity distribution — severity_spec
text: severities satisfy \(X \ge 0\). supported built-models : Exponential: rate > 0, matching stats::dexp(). Gamma: shape > 0, rate > 0, matching stats::dgamma(). Lognormal: meanlog finite sdlog > 0, matching stats::dlnorm(). point mass specified "degenerate". Weibull: shape > 0, scale > 0, matching stats::dweibull(). Pareto II (Lomax): shape > 0, scale > 0; survival function \(P(X>x)=(1+x/\mathrm{scale})^{-\mathrm{shape}}\) \(x \ge 0\). Pareto distribution positive lower endpoint. Burr XII: shape1 > 0, shape2 > 0, scale > 0, survival function \(P(X>x)=[1+(x/\mathrm{scale})^{\mathrm{shape1}}]^{-\mathrm{shape2}}\). Log-logistic: shape > 0, scale > 0, Burr XII special case shape1 = shape, shape2 = 1. Degenerate: value >= 0 finite amount probability one. Finite discrete: values strictly increasing vector distinct finite nonnegative amounts; probs contains strictly positive probabilities, length summing one (numerical tolerance). Amounts need integer multiples common unit. Unlike frequency distribution, individual claim severity may atom zero need absolutely continuous. "degenerate" "discrete" models represented discrete specifications rather forced continuous family. dist = "custom", custom must named list support least one pdf pmf. support list must contain type, lower, upper, type "continuous", "discrete", "lattice", "mixed"; lattice support additionally requires positive step. support component may also function params returning list. mixed specification requires pdf, pmf, cdf. Custom operations, provided, follow interfaces: pdf(x, params, log = FALSE), pmf(x, params, log = FALSE), cdf(q, params, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE), quantile(p, params, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE), rng(n, params), raw_moment(order, params), limited_moment(order, limit, params), mgf(t, params), laplace(t, params). argument params named list collected .... frequency_spec(), constructor checks shape custom definition certify mathematical validity. internal registry supplies probability functions raw moments built-families. advanced operations (example limited moments, MGF heavy-tailed distributions, numerical Laplace transforms) intentionally left unavailable public interfaces set. particular, numerical approximation performed constructor.

title: Pure endowment (discounted survival): \({}_tE_x\) — t_Ex
text: function follows compact actuarial notation used throughout tidyactuarial: lt life table, x age, t duration, interest-rate input, i_type interest-rate type, m conversion frequency nominal rates. pure endowment fundamental building block life contingency mathematics. serves actuarial discount factor, combining financial discounting mortality: $${}_tE_x = v^t \cdot {}_tp_x.$$ Discounted products use original log accumulation rate, retaining representable values annual effective equivalent loses range. actuarial present value, probability: can exceed one negative interest rates capped. equivalent rate tidy output may round -1 overflow, without used valuation. ordinary notation discount factor : $$v = (1+i_e)^{-1}.$$ Key identities involving \({}_nE_x\): Actuarial accumulated value:     \(\ddot{s}_{x:\overline{n}|} = \ddot{}_{x:\overline{n}|} /     {}_nE_x\). Endowment insurance decomposition:     \(A_{x:\overline{n}|} = ^1_{x:\overline{n}|} + {}_nE_x\). Deferred annuity:     \({}_{n|}\ddot{}_x = {}_nE_x \cdot \ddot{}_{x+n}\). constant force mortality \(\mu\) force interest \(\delta\): $${}_nE_x = e^{-n(\mu + \delta)}.$$ variance pure endowment random variable : $$\mathrm{Var}(Z) = v^{2n} \cdot {}_np_x \cdot {}_nq_x.$$

title: t-year survival probability from a life table — t_px
text: integer-year survival obtained directly life table (Finan, Section 22): $${}_n p_x = \frac{\ell_{x+n}}{\ell_x}$$ non-integer durations, let \(t = n + s\) \(n = \lfloor t \rfloor\) \(s \[0,1)\). (Finan, Section 24): $${}_t p_x = {}_n p_x \times {}_s p_{x+n}$$ fractional-year factor \({}_s p_y\) depends assumption: UDD (Finan, Sec. 24.1): \({}_s p_y = 1 - s \times q_y\) CF (Finan, Sec. 24.2): \({}_s p_y = (p_y)^s\) Balducci (Finan, Sec. 24.3):     \({}_s p_y = \frac{p_y}{1 - (1 - s) \times q_y}\) Missing annual survival probabilities derived directly adjacent survivor counts, avoiding cancellation \(1-q_y\). CF Balducci retain logarithmic survival count ratio underflows. Supplied px values remain use; input columns describe consistent annual life table. \(x + t > \omega\) (terminal age), function returns 0 established table-horizon convention, including open tables. truncation, inference survival beyond observed ages; extend table evaluating longer horizon. Interval tables nonannual widths km_lifetable require annual conversion first.

title: Two-life survival probability for independent lives — t_pxy
text: Independence assumed throughout (Finan, Sections 56–57). **Joint-life status** (Finan, Section 56): status survives long lives alive. $${}_tp_{xy} = {}_tp_x \cdot {}_tp_y.$$ **Last-survivor status** (Finan, Section 57): status survives long least one life alive. $${}_tp_{\overline{xy}} = {}_tp_x + {}_tp_y - {}_tp_x \cdot {}_tp_y.$$ Individual survival probabilities \({}_tp_x\) \({}_tp_y\) use observed lx ratios fractional survival UDD, constant force, Balducci (Finan, Section 24). Logarithmic calculations retain small annual survival without subtracting rounded death probability one. Last-survivor survival evaluated \(\max(p_x,p_y)+(1-\max(p_x,p_y))\min(p_x,p_y)\). Tables must unique consecutive annual integer ages finite, nonnegative, nonincreasing lx. Supplied px/qx must lie [0,1] agree observed annual lx ratios within 1e-10; unknown probabilities may NA. Ages must fit R's integer range durations must finite. established t_px horizon zero-duration conventions apply; survival beyond last recorded age truncation, extrapolation.

title: Two-life survival probability for independent lives — t_pxy
code: lt <- data.frame(   x  = 60:66,   lx = c(100000, 99000, 97500, 95500, 93000, 90000, 86000) )  # Joint life, 2.5 years, UDD (Finan, Sec. 56) t_pxy(lt, x = 60, y = 62, t = 2.5, frac = "UDD", status = "joint") #> [1] 0.9056154  # Verify: joint = product of marginals t_px(lt, x = 60, t = 2.5, frac = "UDD") *   t_px(lt, x = 62, t = 2.5, frac = "UDD") #> [1] 0.9056154  # Last survivor, 2.5 years, constant force (Finan, Sec. 57) t_pxy(lt, x = 60, y = 62, t = 2.5, frac = "CF", status = "last") #> [1] 0.9978385  # Same result if the same table is supplied explicitly for both lives t_pxy(list(lt, lt), x = 60, y = 62, t = 2.5, frac = "UDD", status = "joint") #> [1] 0.9056154  # Different life tables for the two lives lt_m <- data.frame(   x  = 60:66,   lx = c(100000, 98500, 96800, 94800, 92400, 89500, 86000) ) lt_f <- data.frame(   x  = 60:66,   lx = c(100000, 99000, 97800, 96400, 94700, 92700, 90300) ) t_pxy(list(lt_m, lt_f), x = 60, y = 62, t = 2.5, frac = "UDD", status = "joint") #> [1] 0.9178384  # Finan Example 56.2 style: integer survival # 10_p_{50:60} = 10_p_50 * 10_p_60 lt_ilt <- data.frame(   x  = 50:70,   lx = c(8950901, 8879913, 8804189, 8723382, 8637048,          8544731, 8445974, 8340310, 8227261, 8106334,          7977338, 7839775, 7693040, 7536522, 7369603,          7191658, 7002051, 6800139, 6585264, 6356752,          6114913) ) t_pxy(lt_ilt, x = 50, y = 60, t = 10, status = "joint") #> [1] 0.6831617  # Finan Problem 56.1: t_q_xy = t_q_x + t_q_y - t_q_x * t_q_y p_joint <- t_pxy(lt, x = 60, y = 62, t = 3, status = "joint") q_joint <- 1 - p_joint qx <- 1 - t_px(lt, x = 60, t = 3) qy <- 1 - t_px(lt, x = 62, t = 3) c(q_joint = q_joint, q_sum = qx + qy - qx * qy)  # should match #>   q_joint     q_sum  #> 0.1184615 0.1184615

title: t-year death probability from a life table — t_qx
text: Uses t_px input horizon conventions; identity : $${}_t q_x = 1 - {}_t p_x.$$ Small fractional losses formed directly subtracting one, preserving probabilities whose survival rounds one. identity \({}_tq_x = {}_td_x / \ell_x\) (Finan, Section 22) holds integer \(t\), \({}_td_x = \ell_x - \ell_{x+t}\) expected number deaths ages \(x\) \(x+t\). fractional durations, result depends chosen assumption (UDD, CF, Balducci); see t_px details formulas (Finan, Section 24). deferred death probability \({}_{n|}q_x\) can obtained (Finan, Section 23.4): $${}_{n|}q_x = {}_np_x \cdot q_{x+n} = {}_{n+1}q_x - {}_nq_x.$$

text: Let \(q_x^{(j)}\) annual decrement probability cause \(j\) \(q_x^{(\tau)}\) total decrement probability. integer \(t\), $$ {}_t q_x^{(j)} = \sum_{k=0}^{t-1} \left(\prod_{r=0}^{k-1} p_{x+r}^{(\tau)}\right) q_{x+k}^{(j)}. $$ non-integer \(t = n + s\) \(n = \lfloor t \rfloor\) \(s \[0,1)\), function supports fractional-age assumptions specified frac uses additional convention within-year cause proportions remain constant: \({}_s q_x^{(j)} = w_j \, {}_s q_x^{(\tau)}\) \(w_j = q_x^{(j)} / q_x^{(\tau)}\) (0 \(q_x^{(\tau)}=0\)). Supported fractional-age assumptions total decrement: "UDD": \({}_s q_x^{(\tau)} = s q_x^{(\tau)}\). "CF":  \({}_s p_x^{(\tau)} = (p_x^{(\tau)})^s\). "Balducci": \({}_s q_x^{(\tau)} = \frac{s q_x^{(\tau)}}{1-(1-s)q_x^{(\tau)}}\).
